sections.heading: C — License types, ID documents
sections.markdown:
## C — License types, ID documents

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
A regular Class D credential at age sixteen or older covers personal vehicles up to twenty-six thousand pounds [A01].
Why it matters: age plus weight limit defines the baseline car privilege.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Applicants younger than nineteen need approved driver education or an out-of-state or out-of-country license, and drivers under twenty-one receive a provisional Class D under a separate point system [A01].
Why it matters: teen path and provisional status are exam traps.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
A limited-term credential goes to a non-citizen with verified lawful status that qualifies for REAL ID, while a driving privilege card covers a parolee or other lawfully present person ineligible for REAL ID and an undocumented immigrant [A01].
Why it matters: lawful-status category selects the certificate type.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
A driving privilege card is for driving only and is not valid identification or age verification, it expires each year on the holder birthday, and no temporary card or drive time is allowed before the plastic card arrives by mail [A01].
Why it matters: DPC limits plus yearly expiry plus mail wait are frequently tested.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A05
An original license generally expires on the holder birthday eight years after issue when over twenty-one, while a provisional license issued under age twenty-one expires on the holder birthday five years after issue [A05].
Why it matters: eight-year versus five-year validity is a numeric discriminator.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A05
A visitor with a valid out-of-state or out-of-country license may drive in Utah for up to six months, an out-of-state learner permit does not allow driving in Utah, and an out-of-state license must be surrendered when applying for Utah [A05].
Why it matters: visitor window plus permit exclusion plus surrender rule.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A06
Renewal may be sought up to six months before expiration with a new eight-year license from the birthday after issue, the good-driver online extension needs no more than six reportable violations in eight years with valid status, and change of address needs notice within ten days for Class D [A06].
Why it matters: renewal window, good-driver count, and ten-day address rule carry numbers.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A02
Class A and Class B concern combined or single vehicles over twenty-six thousand one pounds with a towed unit over ten thousand one pounds and intrastate limits at ages eighteen to twenty, Class C covers smaller buses and hazmat at minimum age twenty-one, and Class D covers other non-motorcycle vehicles at minimum age sixteen [A02].
Why it matters: weight plus trailer plus age table separates the classes.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A04
A regular Class D or ID identity showing needs one of a valid unexpired passport or card, a state-certified birth certificate, a consular birth-abroad report, a permanent resident card, or a naturalization or citizenship certificate, with hospital, miniature, laminated, or photocopied birth records rejected [A04].
Why it matters: acceptable-versus-rejected identity list is a checklist question.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A80
Social security showing needs a signed government card or else a W-2, SSA-1099, non-SSA-1099, pay stub, or an agency ineligibility letter tied to lawful presence status [A80].
Why it matters: backup SSN proofs plus card-stub exclusion matter.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A81
Utah residence and mailing showing needs two documents bearing name and address and dated within ninety days, drawn from bank statement, court papers, mortgage or rental contract, major credit-card bill, property-tax notice, school transcript, utility bill, or vehicle title [A81].
Why it matters: two-document plus ninety-day freshness rule is high yield.
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A82
First Utah license proof of driving experience means driver-education completion when under nineteen, or else an existing driving privilege from another state or country, and it is not required for a learner permit or ID card [A82].
Why it matters: experience proof versus permit exception is confusable.
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A83
For limited-term identity and lawful-status proof, supply one unexpired document: either a DHS employment authorization document, verified through SAVE, or a foreign passport with a valid visa and I-ninety-four, also verified through SAVE [A83].
Why it matters: SAVE verification plus status-paper step distinguishes limited-term.
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A84
A driving privilege card needs one primary paper such as a foreign birth certificate or unexpired foreign passport with translation when needed, plus one secondary paper such as church, court, school, employee, insurance, consular, voter, license, or prior DPC records, plus SSN or ITIN proof and a sealed fingerprint card with photo for an original [A84][S84_0].
Why it matters: two-layer identity plus fingerprint packet is unique to DPC.
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A06
Only a Utah resident may hold an ID card, and Utah law forbids holding a license certificate and an ID card at the same time [A06].
Why it matters: residency plus no-dual-holding rule is a clean binary test point.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A03
Office-visit papers must be originals or agency-certified copies with faxed or photocopied papers refused, any name difference needs a legal name-change paper, and a returned check costs a twenty-dollar service charge to keep the privilege [A03].
Why it matters: original-document plus name-paper plus fee penalty are procedure traps.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0023]
